APCO 1P00.subject: APCO
APCO 1P00.title: Introduction to Media Computation
APCO 1P00.description: Programming by example, designing and debugging of programs, encoding and manipulation of text and graphics, file processing, simple HTML and automatic generation, and manipulating and parsing of web pages.
APCO 1P00.format: Lectures, 3 hours per week; lab, 2 hours per week; tutorial, 1 hour per week.
APCO 1P00.restriction: not open to COSC (single or combined), BCB, CAST, CNET and DASA majors.
notes: prior computer experience is not required. This course may be offered in multiple modes of delivery. The method of delivery will be listed on the academic timetable, in the applicable term.

APCO 1P01.subject: APCO
APCO 1P01.title: Fluency With Technology
APCO 1P01.description: Skills, concepts and capabilities of computers, networks and the Internet. Topics include representation of information, current hardware, software and network technologies, modelling with Excel, presentations with PowerPoint, Internet searching and basic web page development with HTML.
APCO 1P01.format: Lectures, 3 hours per week; lab, 2 hours per week.
APCO 1P01.restriction: not open to COSC (single or combined), BCB, CAST, CNET and DASA majors.
notes: some prior computer experience is preferred but not required. This course may be offered in multiple modes of delivery. The method of delivery will be listed on the academic timetable, in the applicable term.

APCO 1P30.subject: APCO
APCO 1P30.title: Programming for Interactive Media
APCO 1P30.description: Introduction to contemporary programming syntax including for classes, functions, properties and events for developing interactive media applications.
APCO 1P30.restriction: open to IASC (single or combined) and GAMD majors until date specified in Registration guide. Not open to COSC (single or combined), BCB, CAST, CNET and DASA majors.
notes: enrolment limited to 60 students. This course may be offered in multiple modes of delivery. The method of delivery will be listed on the academic timetable, in the applicable term.

APCO 1P50.subject: APCO
APCO 1P50.title: Integrity and Literacy in the Information Age
APCO 1P50.description: Issues in use of information technology including historic and social perspectives; legal, ethical and moral issues; intellectual property, licensing and copyright; privacy and freedom of expression; professional conduct and information literacy.
APCO 1P50.format: Lectures, 3 hours per week; seminar, 1.5 hours per week.
notes: this course involves seminars and considerable written work. A good command of written and spoken English is required. This course may be offered in multiple modes of delivery. The method of delivery will be listed on the academic timetable, in the applicable term.

APCO 1P93.subject: APCO
APCO 1P93.title: Applied Programming
APCO 1P93.description: Modern software techniques including problem solving and design of effective algorithms, structured program design methodology, subprogram library usage, documentation, correctness, floating-point arithmetic and error analysis.
APCO 1P93.format: Lectures, 3 hours per week; lab, 2 hours per week; tutorial, 1 hour per week.
APCO 1P93.restriction: not open to COSC (single or combined), BCB, CAST, CNET and DASA majors.
notes: this course may be offered in multiple modes of delivery. The method of delivery will be listed on the academic timetable, in the applicable term.

APCO 2P11.subject: APCO
APCO 2P11.title: Personal Computers and Networks
APCO 2P11.description: Inner workings of modern computers from a user's point of view. Understanding the hardware, network and system software. Topics include CPUs, memory, video, input/output, networks, security, installation of operating systems and hands-on trouble shooting.
APCO 2P11.format: Lectures, 3 hours per week; lab, 3 hours per week.
APCO 2P11.restriction: open to APCO minors until date specified in Registration guide.
notes: this course may be offered in multiple modes of delivery. The method of delivery will be listed on the academic timetable, in the applicable term.
Completion of this course will replace previous assigned grade and credit obtained in APCO 2P01.

APCO 2P61.subject: APCO
APCO 2P61.title: Website Creation
APCO 2P61.description: Creative approaches to basic technical and design foundations of website design and development. Processing and management of images and other media assets, structuring websites, development tools and applications, web hosting and dissemination strategies. Contemporary web-based art practices within the broader history of cultural production.

prerequisites.raw: VISA 1P95 (minimum 60 percent) and 1P96 (minimum 60 percent) or permission of the instructor

APCO 2P61.restriction: open to STAC, VISA (single or combined) and VISA (Honours)/BEd (Intermediate/Senior) majors until date specified in Registration guide. After that date open to STAC, VISA (single or combined), VISA (Honours)/BEd (Intermediate/Senior) majors and APCO minors.
notes: students will need additional materials, which they must supply. Field trips may be required. Students are expected to pay their own expenses. VISA 1P95 recommended. Due to space limitations, audits are not permitted in studio classes. This course may be offered in multiple modes of delivery. The method of delivery will be listed on the academic timetable, in the applicable term.

APCO 2P89.subject: APCO
APCO 2P89.title: Internet Technologies
APCO 2P89.description: Concepts and techniques for building and maintaining advanced interactive Web sites. Topics include XML and SGML, database connectivity and forms handling, basic animation, graphics optimization for the Web, scripting, advanced searching and Web design for accessibility.
APCO 2P89.format: Lectures, 3 hours per week; lab/seminar, 2 hours per week.

prerequisites.raw: APCO 1P00 (minimum 60 percent) and 1P01 (minimum 60 percent) or COSC 1P03 (minimum 60 percent)

notes: this course may be offered in multiple modes of delivery. The method of delivery will be listed on the academic timetable, in the applicable term.

APCO 2P99.subject: APCO
APCO 2P99.title: Project in Applied Computing
APCO 2P99.description: Development project in computing, Internet programming or directed reading essay under the supervision of a faculty member.
notes: students may propose their own projects for departmental approval or may apply for a project proposed by a faculty member. Further information (including project guidelines and project list) is available on the department Web pages. This course may be offered in multiple modes of delivery. The method of delivery will be listed on the academic timetable, in the applicable term.

APCO 3P94.subject: APCO
APCO 3P94.title: Human Computer Interaction
APCO 3P94.description: Human factors in the design and support of computing systems. Design methodologies such as GOMS, TAGs and Task Analysis. Design principles relating to various interaction paradigms.
APCO 3P94.format: Lectures, 3 hours per week; lab/seminar, 2 hours per week.

prerequisites.raw: two credits from APCO (minimum 60 percent), COSC (minimum 60 percent), IASC (minimum 60 percent)

notes: this course may be offered in multiple modes of delivery. The method of delivery will be listed on the academic timetable, in the applicable term.
COMPUTER SCIENCE COURSES

COSC 1P02.subject: COSC
COSC 1P02.title: Introduction to Computer Science
COSC 1P02.description: Foundations of Computer Science and computer programming in a high-level language. Topics include computer fundamentals, representation of information, problem solving and software development, programming language syntax and semantics, methods, input/output, control structures and data types.
COSC 1P02.format: Lectures, 3 hours per week; lab, 2 hours per week; tutorial, 1 hour per week.
notes: This course may be offered in multiple modes of delivery. The method of delivery will be listed on the academic timetable, in the applicable term.

COSC 1P03.subject: COSC
COSC 1P03.title: Introduction to Data Structures
COSC 1P03.description: Programming and problem solving in a high-level programming language. Data structures including arrays and linked-lists. Modularity, abstraction and abstract data types including stacks, queues and lists. Introduction to searching and sorting, recursion, algorithm analysis and object-orientation.
COSC 1P03.format: Lectures, 3 hours per week; lab, 2 hours per week; tutorial, 1 hour per week.
notes: this course may be offered in multiple modes of delivery. The method of delivery will be listed on the academic timetable, in the applicable term.

COSC 1P50.subject: COSC
COSC 1P50.title: Integrity and Literacy in the Information Age
COSC 1P50.description: Issues in use of information technology including historic and social perspectives; legal, ethical and moral issues; intellectual property, licensing and copyright; privacy and freedom of expression; professional conduct and information literacy.
COSC 1P50.format: Lectures, 3 hours per week; seminar, 1.5 hours per week.
notes: this course involves seminars and considerable written work. A good command of written and spoken English is required. This course may be offered in multiple modes of delivery. The method of delivery will be listed on the academic timetable, in the applicable term.

COSC 1P71.subject: COSC
COSC 1P71.title: Essentials of Artificial Intelligence
COSC 1P71.description: Introductory, non-technical survey of artificial intelligence (AI) basics. Historical review of AI, from early approaches to contemporary technologies. Critical overview of successes and limitations. Ethical ramifications of AI, including its risks and safety, impact on society, industry, science, as well as problems arising from bias and misuse.
notes: this course may be offered in multiple modes of delivery. The method of delivery will be listed on the academic timetable, in the applicable term.

COSC 2P03.subject: COSC
COSC 2P03.title: Advanced Data Structures
COSC 2P03.description: Implementation and use of advanced data structures including trees, graphs, hash tables and advanced list structures, sorting and searching, recursion and traversals. Analysis of algorithms.
COSC 2P03.format: Lectures, 3 hours per week; lab, 2 hours per week; tutorial, 1 hour per week.
COSC 2P03.restriction: open to COSC (single or combined), BCB, CAST, CNET, GAMP and NEUR Neurocomputing stream majors.
notes: this course may be offered in multiple modes of delivery. The method of delivery will be listed on the academic timetable, in the applicable term.

COSC 2P05.subject: COSC
COSC 2P05.title: Programming Languages
COSC 2P05.description: Fundamental concepts of programming languages including syntax, semantics, program translation, virtual machines, control, data types, multi-threading, exception handling and abstraction mechanisms. Introduction to programming paradigms including imperative, applicative, logic and object-oriented.
notes: this course may be offered in multiple modes of delivery. The method of delivery will be listed on the academic timetable, in the applicable term.
Completion of this course will replace previous assigned grade and credit obtained in COSC 2P90 and 3P05.

COSC 2P08.subject: COSC
COSC 2P08.title: Programming for Big Data
COSC 2P08.description: Introduction to Python programming and its Data Science ecosystem; handling and analyzing large datasets; data visualization; integrating Python into big data ecosystems; hands-on exercises and projects.
COSC 2P08.format: Lectures, 3 hours per week; lab, 1 hour per week.

COSC 2P12.subject: COSC
COSC 2P12.title: Introduction to Computer Architecture
COSC 2P12.description: Evolution of digital computer. Computer organization including functional units, instruction cycle, control, buses and memory. Instruction types and memory access, instruction sequencing and call/return. Basic assembly language programming.
COSC 2P12.format: Lectures, 3 hours per week; lab, 2 hours per week.
notes: this course may be offered in multiple modes of delivery. The method of delivery will be listed on the academic timetable, in the applicable term.

COSC 2P13.subject: COSC
COSC 2P13.title: Introduction to Operating Systems
COSC 2P13.description: Operating systems and management principles of computing resources and processing. Resource sharing including file, processor, I/O and memory management. Concurrency including: context switching, interprocess communication, and synchronization. Protection and security including encryption. Distributed systems including synchronization algorithms and fundamentals of computer networks.

prerequisites.raw: COSC 2P03 (minimum 60 percent) for COSC (single or combined), BCB, CAST, CNET and NEUR neurocomputing majors; COSC 2P03 (minimum 60 percent), CPCF 1F25 and IASC 2P04 for GAMP majors

expr.text: COSC 2P03 (minimum 60 percent) for COSC (single or combined), BCB, CAST, CNET and NEUR neurocomputing majors; COSC 2P03 (minimum 60 percent), CPCF 1F25 and IASC 2P04 for GAMP majors

notes: this course may be offered in multiple modes of delivery. The method of delivery will be listed on the academic timetable, in the applicable term.

COSC 2P89.subject: COSC
COSC 2P89.title: Internet Technologies
COSC 2P89.description: Concepts and techniques required for building and maintaining advanced interactive Web sites. Topics include XML and SGML, database connectivity and forms handling, basic animation, graphics optimization for the Web, scripting, advanced searching, Web design for accessibility.
COSC 2P89.format: Lectures, 3 hours per week; lab/seminar, 2 hours per week.

prerequisites.raw: COSC 1P03 (minimum 60 percent) or APCO 1P00 (minimum 60 percent) and 1P01 (minimum 60 percent)

notes: this course may be offered in multiple modes of delivery. The method of delivery will be listed on the academic timetable, in the applicable term.

COSC 2P95.subject: COSC
COSC 2P95.title: Programming in C++ with Applications
COSC 2P95.description: C++ as a second language. Basic language structure, data structures, libraries for application. Introduction to object-orientation and UNIX commands.
COSC 2P95.format: Lectures, 3 hours per week; labs 2 hours per week.
notes: students should select the lab appropriate for their application domain (Computer Science or Mathematics). This course may be offered in multiple modes of delivery. The method of delivery will be listed on the academic timetable, in the applicable term.

COSC 2P96.subject: COSC
COSC 2P96.title: Introduction to 3D Modelling and Animation
COSC 2P96.description: Concepts and skills of 3D modelling and rendering using Autodesk Maya. Approaches to building models, using texturizing, lighting, cameras and rendering as well as basic animation techniques. Relevant historical and theoretical perspectives on 3D and virtuality situating 3D within creative process and broader critical practices in cultural production.

prerequisites.raw: one of four COSC credits, IASC 1F01 (1F00), one credit from VISA 1P93 (minimum 60 percent), 1P94 (minimum 60 percent), 1P95 (minimum 60 percent), 1P96 (minimum 60 percent)

expr.text: one of four COSC credits, IASC 1F01 (1F00), one credit from VISA 1P93 (minimum 60 percent), 1P94 (minimum 60 percent), 1P95 (minimum 60 percent), 1P96 (minimum 60 percent)

COSC 2P96.restriction: open to COSC (single or combined), IASC (single or combined), STAC, VISA (single or combined) and VISA (Honours)/BEd (Intermediate/Senior) majors until date specified in Registration guide.
notes: students will need additional materials and equipment, which they must supply. Field trips may be required. Students are expected to pay their own expenses. VISA 1P95 recommended. Due to space limitations, audits are not permitted in studio classes. This course may be offered in multiple modes of delivery. The method of delivery will be listed on the academic timetable, in the applicable term.
Completion of this course will replace previous assigned grade and credit obtained in IASC 2P96.

COSC 3P01.subject: COSC
COSC 3P01.title: Computer Networking
COSC 3P01.description: Principles of computer network: basic networking issues, concepts and solution approaches. Protocol stack and encapsulation including ISO-OSI and TCP/IP models. Application layer including common applications. Transport layer including reliable and unreliable delivery. Network layer including addressing, routing and datagram forwarding. Link layer including MAC addressing and fundamentals on access control. Network programming including client/server programming designs.

prerequisites.raw: COSC 2P03 (minimum of 60 percent) and COSC 2P13 (minimum of 60 percent)

notes: this course may be offered in multiple modes of delivery. The method of delivery will be listed on the academic timetable, in the applicable term.

COSC 3P03.subject: COSC
COSC 3P03.title: Algorithms
COSC 3P03.description: Design and analysis of computer algorithms. Topics include asymptotic notations, solving recurrences, order statistics, general algorithm design techniques such as divide-and-conquer, greedy algorithms, dynamic programming, backtracking and branch-and-bound. Graph and string algorithms. Introduction to NP-Completeness and complexity theory.
notes: this course may be offered in multiple modes of delivery. The method of delivery will be listed on the academic timetable, in the applicable term.

COSC 3P32.subject: COSC
COSC 3P32.title: Database Systems
COSC 3P32.description: Fundamental database concepts: specification, design and applications; various models including the relational model; normal forms, efficiency considerations, queries using SQL, database administration and security. Practical experience in a group project.
COSC 3P32.format: Lectures, 3 hours per week; lab, 2 hours per week.
notes: this course may be offered in multiple modes of delivery. The method of delivery will be listed on the academic timetable, in the applicable term.
Completion of this course will replace previous assigned grade and credit obtained in COSC 2P32.

COSC 3P71.subject: COSC
COSC 3P71.title: Artificial Intelligence
COSC 3P71.description: Historic and philosophical foundations of AI; knowledge representation and reasoning; problem spaces; blind and heuristic search; adversarial search in game playing; machine learning; social and ethical considerations.
COSC 3P71.format: Lectures, 3 hours per week; tutorial, 1 hour per week.
notes: this course may be offered in multiple modes of delivery. The method of delivery will be listed on the academic timetable, in the applicable term.

COSC 3P90.subject: COSC
COSC 3P90.title: Software Development
COSC 3P90.description: Introduction to modern software engineering techniques and applications; Contemporary approaches to software development; Generally applicable principles in software engineering; Hands-on applications of software development.
COSC 3P90.format: Lectures, 3 hours per week; Lab, 1 hour per week

COSC 3P91.subject: COSC
COSC 3P91.title: Advanced Object-Oriented Programming
COSC 3P91.description: Topics may include graphical user interfaces, animation, sound, music, networking, parallelism, client-server and XML using game design as an example. Object-oriented program design including UML and design patterns. Introduction to advanced Java APIs.
COSC 3P91.format: Lectures, 3 hours per week; lab 2 hours per week.
notes: this course may be offered in multiple modes of delivery. The method of delivery will be listed on the academic timetable, in the applicable term.
Completion of this course will replace previous assigned grade and credit obtained in COSC 3P40.

COSC 3P92.subject: COSC
COSC 3P92.title: Computer Architecture
COSC 3P92.description: Topics include buses, internal and external memory, I/O and interfacing, computer arithmetic, instruction sets, RISCs, microprogrammed control, parallel organization.
notes: this course may be offered in multiple modes of delivery. The method of delivery will be listed on the academic timetable, in the applicable term.

COSC 3P93.subject: COSC
COSC 3P93.title: Parallel Computing
COSC 3P93.description: Origins of parallelism, classification of designs, characterization of performance. Pipelined computers: selection and comparison, case studies. Processor arrays: switching networks, case studies. Parallel languages: general principles, parallel constructs, vectorizing compilers, issues of portability. Practical exposure to a parallel programming language and parallel computing hardware. Parallel algorithms: general principles, recurrences, parallel approach to data structures and computational structures. Future trends: technology, design limitations, future supercomputers.
notes: this course may be offered in multiple modes of delivery. The method of delivery will be listed on the academic timetable, in the applicable term.

COSC 3P94.subject: COSC
COSC 3P94.title: Human Computer Interaction
COSC 3P94.description: Human factors in the design and support of computing systems. Design methodologies such as GOMS, TAGs and Task Analysis. Design principles relating to various interaction paradigms.
COSC 3P94.format: Lectures, 3 hours per week; lab/seminar, 2 hours per week.

prerequisites.raw: two credits from APCO (minimum 60 percent), COSC (minimum 60 percent), IASC (minimum 60 percent)

notes: this course may be offered in multiple modes of delivery. The method of delivery will be listed on the academic timetable, in the applicable term.

COSC 3P95.subject: COSC
COSC 3P95.title: Software Analysis and Testing
COSC 3P95.description: Principles of software development besides programming, such as static and dynamic analysis, debugging, diagnosing bugs, and testing. Topics include fundamental properties of software analysis and testing techniques, program analysis and code inspection, defect tracking, causality analysis, software measurement, software profiling, software tracing, acceptance testing, integration testing, regression testing, and performance testing.
COSC 3P95.restriction: open to COSC (single or combined), BCB, CAST, GAMP, and NEUR majors.

COSC 3P96.subject: COSC
COSC 3P96.title: Machine Learning
COSC 3P96.description: Fundamental machine learning techniques with emphasis on using these techniques to design and implement small practical learning systems. Topics include learning as a search, inductive bias, concept learning, computational learning, explanation-based learning and reinforcement learning.
notes: this course may be offered in multiple modes of delivery. The method of delivery will be listed on the academic timetable, in the applicable term.

COSC 3P97.subject: COSC
COSC 3P97.title: Mobile Computing
COSC 3P97.description: Overview of mobile applications, technologies and communication. Common paradigms in mobile computing. Application frameworks and application development. Interaction styles for user interface.
COSC 3P97.restriction: open to COSC (single or combined), BCB, CAST and CNET majors.
notes: this course may be offered in multiple modes of delivery. The method of delivery will be listed on the academic timetable, in the applicable term.
Completion of this course will replace previous assigned grade and credit obtained in COSC 3V97.

COSC 3P98.subject: COSC
COSC 3P98.title: Computer Graphics
COSC 3P98.description: Topics include 2-D and 3-D graphics, curve and surface fitting, light and colour models, real time interfaces, animation and hardware issues (knowledge of C assumed).

prerequisites.raw: COSC 2P03 (minimum 60 percent), three COSC credits and MATH 1P12

notes: this course may be offered in multiple modes of delivery. The method of delivery will be listed on the academic timetable, in the applicable term.

COSC 3P99.subject: COSC
COSC 3P99.title: Computing Project
COSC 3P99.description: Half-year development project or directed reading essay under faculty supervision.
COSC 3P99.restriction: open to COSC (single or combined), BCB, CAST, CNET, GAMP and NEUR Neurocomputing stream majors with a minimum 75 percent major average (or permission of project supervisor) and permission of project coordinator.
notes: students may propose their own projects for departmental approval or may apply for a project proposed by a faculty member. Further information (including project guidelines and project list) is available on the department Web pages. This course may be offered in multiple modes of delivery. The method of delivery will be listed on the academic timetable, in the applicable term.

COSC 3Q95.subject: COSC
COSC 3Q95.title: Internship in Game Programming
COSC 3Q95.description: Internship in a business related to the gaming industry.

prerequisites.raw: COSC 2P03 (minimum 60 percent) and permission of Game Programming Director

COSC 3Q95.restriction: open to GAMP majors and permission of the Game Program Director.
notes: application required. Enrolment will be limited to the number of placements available. Students will be required to attend orientation meetings, occasional meetings with the Student Support Co-ordinator and develop professional learning objectives. Additional components typically include a site visit, a work term report and an employer performance evaluation. This course may be offered in multiple modes of delivery. The method of delivery will be listed on the academic timetable, in the applicable term.

COSC 3V90-3V99.subject: COSC
COSC 3V90-3V99.title: Computing Topics I
COSC 3V90-3V99.restriction: open to COSC (single or combined), BCB, CAST, CNET, GAMP and NEUR Neurocomputing stream majors.

COSC 4F90.subject: COSC
COSC 4F90.title: Computing Project
COSC 4F90.description: Full-year project under the supervision of a faculty member.
COSC 4F90.restriction: open to COSC (single or combined), BCB, CAST and CNET majors with a minimum 75 percent major average, a minimum 10.0 overall credits and permission of project co-ordinator.
notes: students may propose their own projects for departmental approval or may apply for a project proposed by a faculty member. This course is strongly recommended for students considering graduate school. Students must consult with faculty at the end of year 3 regarding supervision of projects. Further information (including project guidelines and project list) is available on the department Web pages. This course may be offered in multiple modes of delivery. The method of delivery will be listed on the academic timetable, in the applicable term.

COSC 4P01.subject: COSC
COSC 4P01.title: Software Engineering 1
COSC 4P01.description: Theory of software engineering. Topics include plan-driven development, Agile development, software requirements elicitation and presentation, verification of software correctness, redundancy, robustness, safety and security. Creation of robust software requirements document. Introduction to tools such as Git and Azure DevOps.
COSC 4P01.format: Lectures, 3 hours per week; tutorial, 1 hour per week.
COSC 4P01.restriction: open to COSC (single or combined), BCB and CAST majors with a minimum of 14.0 overall credits.
notes: this course may be offered in multiple modes of delivery. The method of delivery will be listed on the academic timetable, in the applicable term.
Completion of this course will replace previous assigned grade and credit obtained in COSC 4F00.

COSC 4P02.subject: COSC
COSC 4P02.title: Software Engineering 2
COSC 4P02.description: Application of software engineering. The development of a large-scale software engineering project in a competitive team setting, including creation of complete documentation for a working system.
COSC 4P02.format: Lectures, Seminars, Project Consultation, 3 hours per week.
COSC 4P02.restriction: open to COSC (single or combined), BCB and CAST majors.
notes: this course may be offered in multiple modes of delivery. The method of delivery will be listed on the academic timetable, in the applicable term.
Completion of this course will replace previous assigned grade and credit obtained in COSC 4F00.

COSC 4P03.subject: COSC
COSC 4P03.title: Advanced Algorithms
COSC 4P03.description: Classical and evolving problems and algorithms in Computer Science. Topics include classical design and analysis techniques, cryptography, combinatorics.
notes: this course may be offered in multiple modes of delivery. The method of delivery will be listed on the academic timetable, in the applicable term.

COSC 4P04.subject: COSC
COSC 4P04.title: Graph Drawing and Information Visualization
COSC 4P04.description: Different embeddings, models and representations of graphs and networks, including planar drawing, radial drawing, layered drawing. Algorithms and techniques for network visualization, planarity testing, optimization of graph features such as area or angular resolution. Practical application of network visualization in biology, cartography, data analytics.
notes: this course may be offered in multiple mods of delivery. The method of delivery will be listed on the academic timetable, in the applicable term.

COSC 4P13.subject: COSC
COSC 4P13.title: Operating Systems: Design and Implementation
COSC 4P13.description: Design and implementation of UNIX and other operating systems. Topics include process and thread management, interprocess communication, synchronization and scheduling, multiprocessing, device drivers, kernel memory management, distributed and advanced file systems and STREAMS (knowledge of C assumed).
COSC 4P13.format: Lectures, lab, 3 hours per week; lab, 2 hours per week.
notes: this course may be offered in multiple modes of delivery. The method of delivery will be listed on the academic timetable, in the applicable term.

COSC 4P14.subject: COSC
COSC 4P14.title: Advanced Computer Networks
COSC 4P14.description: Advanced topics in computer networking, including computer network security, wireless and high-speed networking, computer network management and performance evaluation.
COSC 4P14.format: Lectures, 3 hours per week; lab, 2 hours per week.
notes: this course may be offered in multiple modes of delivery. The method of delivery will be listed on the academic timetable, in the applicable term.

COSC 4P32.subject: COSC
COSC 4P32.title: Advanced Database Systems
COSC 4P32.description: Design and implementation of database management systems (DBMS). Topics include: transaction management, crash recovery, query processing algorithms, query optimization, advanced indexing techniques, introductory topics on big data management, and parallel and distributed databases.
notes: this course may be offered in multiple modes of delivery. The method of delivery will be listed on the academic timetable, in the applicable term.

COSC 4P41.subject: COSC
COSC 4P41.title: Functional Programming
COSC 4P41.description: Introduction to functional programming using the languages Haskell and SML. Topics include all data types, type inference, pattern-matching, recursion, polymorphism, higher-order functions, lazy vs eager evaluation, modules and monads.
COSC 4P41.format: Lectures, 3 hours per week; lab, 2 hours per week
notes: this course may be offered in multiple modes of delivery. The method of delivery will be listed on the academic timetable, in the applicable term.

COSC 4P42.subject: COSC
COSC 4P42.title: Formal Methods in Software Engineering
COSC 4P42.description: Specification and correctness of software. Topics include algebraic specifications, semantics of programming languages, Hoare/dynamic logic, specification languages, program transformation.
COSC 4P42.format: Lectures, 3 hours per week; lab, 2 hours per week.
notes: this course may be offered in multiple modes of delivery. The method of delivery will be listed on the academic timetable, in the applicable term.

COSC 4P50.subject: COSC
COSC 4P50.title: Introduction to Cyber Security
COSC 4P50.description: Senior-level course focuses on offensive security and defensive science. Topics include: reconnaissance, scanning, enumeration, exploitation of computer systems and networks, firewalls, intrusion detections and prevention, access control list, encryption, etc.

COSC 4P61.subject: COSC
COSC 4P61.title: Theory of Computation
COSC 4P61.description: Regular languages and finite state machines: deterministic and non-deterministic machines, Kleene's theorem, the pumping lemma, Myhill-Nerode Theorem and decidable questions. Context-free languages: generation by context-free grammars and acceptance by pushdown automata, pumping lemma, closure properties, decidability. Turing machines: recursively enumerable languages, universal Turing machines, halting problem and other undecidable questions.
COSC 4P61.restriction: open to COSC (single or combined), BCB, CAST, CNET, GAMP and NEUR Neurocomputing stream majors.
notes: MATH students may take this course with permission of the Mathematics Department. This course may be offered in multiple modes of delivery. The method of delivery will be listed on the academic timetable, in the applicable term.

COSC 4P78.subject: COSC
COSC 4P78.title: Robotics
COSC 4P78.description: Computer control aspects of robots focusing on behaviour-based robot control architectures. Topics include robot components and subsystems, sensors and perception, object location and manipulation, mobile robot navigation, task planning, control architectures, adaptive and social behaviour.
COSC 4P78.format: Lectures, 2 hours per week; lab, 2 hours per week.
notes: PHYS 1P91 and 1P92 are recommended. This course may be offered in multiple modes of delivery. The method of delivery will be listed on the academic timetable, in the applicable term.

COSC 4P80.subject: COSC
COSC 4P80.title: Artificial Neural Networks
COSC 4P80.description: Practical problem solving using artificial neural networks. Supervised learning, single- and multilayer feed-forward networks and backpropagation and refinements; recurrent neural networks; Hopfield networks and Boltzmann machines. Unsupervised learning, competitive learning, Kohonen map and self-organizing feature maps.
notes: this course may be offered in multiple modes of delivery. The method of delivery will be listed on the academic timetable, in the applicable term.

COSC 4P81.subject: COSC
COSC 4P81.title: AI Programming
COSC 4P81.description: Developing computer applications for AI problem solving. Topics in AI software systems, programming languages and paradigms, and their suitability in different problem domains. Languages relevant to AI programming.
notes: this course may be offered in multiple modes of delivery. The method of delivery will be listed on the academic timetable, in the applicable term.

COSC 4P82.subject: COSC
COSC 4P82.title: Genetic Programming
COSC 4P82.description: Synthesis of computer programs using evolutionary computation. Different representations, including tree, linear, grammatical. Theoretical analyses, including the effects of operators, representations and fitness landscapes. Practical applications in problem solving, decision making, classification, computer vision and design.
notes: this course may be offered in multiple modes of delivery. The method of delivery will be listed on the academic timetable, in the applicable term.

COSC 4P83.subject: COSC
COSC 4P83.title: Reinforcement Learning
COSC 4P83.description: Multi-armed bandits, Markov decision processes, model-based and model-free methods (such as dynamic programming, Monte Carlo methods, and temporal-difference methods) for learning value and policy functions. Approximation solutions including deep reinforcement learning.
COSC 4P83.restriction: open to COSC single or combined, GAME, NEUR, and Data Science programs.
notes: this course may be offered in multiple modes of delivery. The method of delivery will be listed on the academic timetable, in the applicable term.

COSC 4P84.subject: COSC
COSC 4P84.title: Natural Language Processing
COSC 4P84.description: Introduction to the computational modelling of natural language, including techniques and algorithms, formalisms, and applications. Fundamental topics covered include computational morphology, semantics, syntactic parsing, language modelling, summarization, machine translation, coreference resolution, and contemporary machine learning techniques.
notes: this course may be offered in multiple mods of delivery. The method of delivery will be listed on the academic timetable, in the applicable term.

COSC 4P96.subject: COSC
COSC 4P96.title: Topics in Computational Intelligence
COSC 4P96.description: Current methods their practical applications. Emphasis on evolutionary computation, swarm intelligence, artificial immune systems, and neural networks. Applications include optimization, classification, games, swarm robotics, image processing, and network science. Survey and discussion of current literature.
notes: this course may be offered in multiple modes of delivery. The method of delivery will be listed on the academic timetable, in the applicable term.
Completion of this course will replace previous assigned grade and credit obtained in COSC 4V96.
data_quality_notes: Calendar lists this under 'Restriction:' but it reads like a prerequisite; treated as a prerequisite.

COSC 4P98.subject: COSC
COSC 4P98.title: Topics in Computer Media and Digital Audio
COSC 4P98.description: Fractals, digital audio fundamentals, Fourier analysis, MIDI, computer composition, music and sound processing and user interfaces. Programming assignments may use C, Java, Supercollider and Csound.
notes: this course may be offered in multiple modes of delivery. The method of delivery will be listed on the academic timetable, in the applicable term.

COSC 4V80-4V99.title: Computing Topics II
COSC 4V80-4V99.restriction: open to COSC (single or combined), BCB, CAST, CNET, GAMP and NEUR Neurocomputing stream majors.
